summary.intent: Plan and then execute GSD roadmap Phase 69 (FUSE and WinFsp Rust integration with grant-root awareness) for the CipherBox project — a large Rust port phase covering rotation engine, grant-scope gating, and Windows/WinFsp support (requirement TEST-03) — using the GSD plan-phase and execute-phase workflows with research, pattern-mapping, planning, verification, and wave-based parallel worktree-isolated execution.
summary.outcome: Research, validation strategy, and pattern-mapping were completed and committed; all 14 plans (69-01..69-14, 7 waves) were written (recovering from a mid-planning API crash), verified by the plan-checker with no blockers, and coverage-gated (TEST-03 + D-01..D-08). Execution then proceeded wave-by-wave with worktree-isolated subagents and post-merge cargo gates; by the point the transcript ends, Waves 1–3 (8/14 plans: node codec, rotation floor gate, api-client wrapper, node seal/unseal, grant-scope predicate, gated listing, FUSE grant_scope module, rotation engine walk core) were merged clean with all cargo checks/tests passing, and Wave 4 was being set up.

repo: Grant-root scope algorithm (crates/fuse/src/write_ops/grant_scope.rs) has a complete TS reference at packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/scope.ts — it's a port, not design-from-scratch.

GET /shares/sent (SentShareResponseDto in apps/api/src/shares/dto/share-response.dto.ts) has no revoked/status field because shares are hard-deleted on revoke — every row returned is inherently an active grant.
crates/core's build_node_aad fails closed on non-UUID node ids — test fixtures across multiple plans (69-06, 69-08) needed real UUIDv5 strings, not arbitrary test strings.

Cold-child gating must source generation/version_floor from the parent SealedChildRef mirror, never the child's own PublishedNode.generation (Pitfall 4/M1) — verified by a dedicated unit test in crates/sdk/src/listing.rs.

rotate_one in crates/sdk/src/rotation/engine.rs takes parent_read_key as a borrow (&[u8]) specifically so the Rust type system — not just convention — prevents zeroing the caller's key buffer (terminal-owner rule).
The actual desktop E2E GitHub Actions workflow name is 'Desktop E2E Tests', not 'CI E2E Tests' as worded in ROADMAP.md/CONTEXT.md — using the wrong name in gh workflow run would 404.
crates/sdk/src/lib.rs is a shared edit point for multiple rotation/listing plans (69-06 and 69-08 both touch it), forcing serialization within a wave despite otherwise-disjoint work.
Phase 69 CONTEXT_WINDOW=200000 means no 1M-token cross-phase enrichment is available for this phase.

code.finding: rotate_one takes parent_read_key: &[u8] as a borrow to make it impossible to zero the caller's buffer; read_key_prime is only zeroed on rotate_one's own failure paths.

resolve_published_node is pub(crate) only (not pub) per D-05/SC#6 — list_folder/list_shared_folder are the sole gated entrypoints, and RotationHighWater::enforce_resolved always runs before decode/unseal touches fetched bytes.
69-13 explicitly defers the Windows spawn_file_meta_reencrypt caller and the whole-tree SC#2 gate to plan 69-14.

workflow: When a gsd-planner subagent crashes mid-run (API error), check disk directly for how many plans actually landed before restarting — writes-so-far often survive the crash and only the tail plan needs a fresh single-plan-mode spawn, avoiding a full re-plan.

Trust git (merge-base / git log) over an agent's self-reported <worktree_metadata> expected_base or a commit-helper's reported failure status — both have shown false readings (69-06's expected_base was a mis-capture of its own docs commit; commit_failed is a known false-negative when lint-staged actually succeeded).

Canary the first plan of a phase synchronously (not fanned out in parallel) to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline before committing to unattended parallel waves — caught nothing this run but is worth the ~5min cost on high-stakes unattended execution.

Fresh git worktrees can lack node_modules, causing the husky pre-commit hook to fail on first commit (lint-staged not found) — running pnpm install --frozen-lockfile in the worktree fixes it with no code changes needed; this recurred across at least two independent executor subagents.
Running cargo fmt at the crate root inside a worktree can reformat unrelated files as a side effect — executors must diff-scope-check and revert stray formatting before committing.

A literal grep-based 'truths check' (e.g. grep -n 'ecies') can false-positive on doc-comment prose describing what code replaces, even when no matching code exists — reword the comment rather than treat it as a real violation.

For unattended --auto execution, schedule a wakeup and write a durable on-disk handoff file before pausing, so full recovery state survives even if conversation context gets summarized across the pause window.

friction: gsd-planner subagent hit a connection-closed API error mid-run while writing plan 69-14, requiring a paused/resumed recovery flow with a manually authored handoff file.

All 13 initially-written plans used pseudo-IDs (SC-01..SC-06) in their requirements: frontmatter instead of the real phase requirement TEST-03, which would have failed the §13 coverage gate silently until caught.

API-SURFACE.md regeneration (intel hook) returns symbolCount:0/stale:true for this Rust phase since the extractor is TS/JS-focused — effectively a no-op hint that had to be manually recognized and skipped.

A worktree agent (69-06) reported an expected_base in its <worktree_metadata> that was actually its own docs commit rather than the true fork point, requiring a manual git verification step before merge to avoid a bad merge base.
STATE.md/ROADMAP.md update steps (§13b/§13c) after the coverage gates turned out to be idempotent no-ops (already correct), only discovered after running them and checking git status.

The commit helper reported commit_failed for the VALIDATION.md commit and for the final plans commit even though the commits actually landed — a known false-negative that requires manual git log verification each time.
open_items: 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows + TEST-03/SC#5) is marked autonomous:false and requires a Windows box for human verification — the natural hard stop for the --auto execution run.

The SC#6 grep-gate in plans 69-06/69-09 uses a placeholder symbol name (flagged by the plan-checker as non-blocking) that must be confirmed against the real crate-private resolve symbol name at execution/build time.

Desktop E2E workflow naming ('Desktop E2E Tests' vs 'CI E2E Tests') was corrected only within plan 69-14 — the underlying ROADMAP.md/CONTEXT.md wording that caused the discrepancy has not itself been updated.
Execution was still mid-flight (Wave 4 setup, 8/14 plans merged) when the transcript ends — Waves 4-7 including the WinFsp/Windows plan remain to be executed.
SHARE-WRITE-KEY write-share key threading gap (already tracked in prior memory) remains open and wasn't addressed by this phase.
